title: Acts 14:19–28
context: Opponents from Antioch and Iconium win over the crowd, who stone Paul and drag him out of the city, thinking he is dead. As the disciples gather around him, he gets up and goes back into the city, then leaves for Derbe, where many become disciples. Paul and Barnabas return through Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch, strengthening the disciples, urging them to continue in the faith, and telling them that through many hardships we must enter God’s kingdom. They appoint elders with prayer and fasting, then return to Antioch and report how God had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.

verses.text: But some Jews from Antioch and Iconium came there, and having persuaded the multitudes, they stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.
verses.arminianNotes: Jews from Antioch and Iconium persuade the crowd, who stone Paul and leave him for dead. Arminian readers see how quickly praise can turn to violence.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see Paul suffering what he once inflicted on Stephen.

verses.text: But as the disciples stood around him, he rose up, and entered into the city. On the next day he went out with Barnabas to Derbe.
verses.arminianNotes: The disciples gather around him, he rises, and the next day goes to Derbe. Arminian commentators see remarkable endurance.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see God preserving his servant for further work.

verses.text: When they had preached the Good News to that city and had made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
verses.arminianNotes: They preach in Derbe and make many disciples, then return to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch. Arminian readers see courage in going back to dangerous places.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see pastoral care for those God has gathered.

verses.text: strengthening the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that through many afflictions we must enter into God’s Kingdom.
verses.arminianNotes: They strengthen the disciples, exhort them to continue in the faith, and say that through many hardships we must enter the kingdom. Arminian readers see continuing in the faith as a condition believers must meet, which is why it requires exhortation.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see exhortation as the means God uses to secure the perseverance he has promised, and they see suffering as appointed on the way to glory.

verses.text: When they had appointed elders for them in every assembly, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord on whom they had believed.
verses.arminianNotes: They appoint elders in every church with prayer and fasting and commit them to the Lord. Arminian expositors see churches given leadership and entrusted to God.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see a plurality of elders in each church, important for Reformed church order.

verses.text: They passed through Pisidia and came to Pamphylia.
verses.arminianNotes: They pass through Pisidia to Pamphylia. Arminian readers see the journey continuing.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the mission advancing on God’s schedule.

verses.text: When they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
verses.arminianNotes: They preach in Perga and go down to Attalia. Arminian commentators note they now preach where they had passed through earlier.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see the word sown in another city.

verses.text: From there they sailed to Antioch, from where they had been committed to the grace of God for the work which they had fulfilled.
verses.arminianNotes: They sail back to Antioch, where they had been commended to God’s grace. Arminian readers see the mission completed.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the work fulfilled by God’s grace.

verses.text: When they had arrived and had gathered the assembly together, they reported all the things that God had done with them, and that he had opened a door of faith to the nations.
verses.arminianNotes: They report all God had done and how he opened a door of faith to the Gentiles. Arminian expositors see God opening the opportunity for Gentiles to believe.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see God as the one who opened the door, and many in the tradition read this as God granting faith itself.

verses.text: They stayed there with the disciples for a long time.
verses.arminianNotes: They stay a long time with the disciples. Arminian readers see rest and fellowship after hardship.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the church strengthened through their presence.
